title: UDLM Composition Shape
description: The shape of a composition — its constituents and how much of itself it exposes — held once, where anything that composes can reference it. A catalog item is a PROVIDER CLASS (maintainer ruling 2026-08-09: 'a catalog_item is a consumable class defined by the providers or some 3rd party entity ... it could be a template, it could be a single resource class'), so this shape belongs to the class layer rather than to a record kind. Definitions only: no identity, no tenancy, no lifecycle — those belong to whatever carries the composition.

constituents.description: The composite payload declaration (template-composition-model.md §2.1): which constituent resource types make up the service, how they order (depends_on), how data moves between them (bindings), who fulfills each one (provided_by), and how each one's failure affects the composite (failure_effect). component_ids must be unique within the item; depends_on and bindings.from_component must reference sibling component_ids; the depends_on graph must be acyclic (CMP-002/§2.3) — registry/tools/validate.py enforces all three.

component_id.description: Stable local identifier for the constituent within this composite — unique within the item (validate.py-enforced). Used in depends_on references, runtime constituent_status, and transparent-mode uuid derivation (CMP-007).

resource_type.description: Tier-1 vendor-neutral Category.Type name from the Resource Type Registry; single-segment permitted for cross-cutting types — exactly the same name grammar as the realized-entity schema (data-model-core §2). THREE SEGMENTS, not two. The earlier `{0,1}` cap made a composition unable to name a PROVIDER class (`Compute.VM.OCPVirt`) or another TEMPLATE (`Template.Application.AcmeThreeTier`) as a constituent — so nested compositions were structurally impossible while the spec documented them as supported. ADR-038's naming consequence widened four patterns to `{0,2}` and missed this one; the class name pattern in class.schema.json has always allowed three.

type_version.description: Optional pin to a specific Resource Type Specification version. Omitted = the registry's current version at expansion time.

edge_type.description: Whether the composite OWNS this part or merely uses it. Realization needs it: a composite's single constituents[] list fans out into two places on the realized record — an owned part becomes an entry in the System's `constituents[]`, a borrowed one becomes a `dependencies[]` edge carrying this same edge_type. contained_by = the composite creates and owns it; it is a part, and GRP-INV-002 makes it non-overridably co-tenant with the composite. binds_to = the composite uses something that exists and belongs to someone else — a stake in a shared resource, or an activity bound to the stack — which is how a relationship legitimately crosses a tenant boundary, behind a cross-tenant authorization (CTX-001). Defaults to contained_by, which is what every constituent meant before this field existed. `depends_on` and `references` are deliberately not offered: sibling ordering is already the `depends_on` FIELD below, and a pure pointer with no lifecycle coupling is a field value rather than a constituent.
edge_type.$comment: CMP-012 checks the coherence with fulfillment: a BYO resource cannot be owned.

provided_by.description: self = the registering provider fulfills this constituent directly via its standard Services API; external = the control plane's Placement Engine selects a provider at request time (template-composition-model.md §2.2, CMP-006).

fulfillment.description: Who procures this constituent's request content, and when (UDLM ADR-009). platform = the control plane's loop assembles it from consumer_fields at assembly-time (default); provider = the realizing provider brokers a sub-intent THROUGH the control plane at realize-time, contributing realization-time specifics via a binding; consumer = the consumer supplies an existing resource reference (BYO). Orthogonal to provided_by (the realizer axis) — fulfillment is the procurement axis. The control plane always orchestrates and applies policy + cycle detection regardless of mode.

depends_on.description: Sibling component_ids whose realized state must exist before this constituent can be dispatched — the ordering edges within the item (template-composition-model.md §2.3). The graph must be acyclic; forward topological order = dispatch, reverse = compensation/decommission. Sibling resolution and cycle rejection are validate.py-enforced.

bindings.description: DECLARED data movement (data-model-core §4): values pulled from a producer constituent's typed realized outputs into this constituent's spec at dispatch time. This is the typed, declared equivalent of the control plane control-plane's CEL ${component.output} wiring — data movement, not transformation (T4). A binding's from_component MUST also appear in this constituent's depends_on: data movement implies ordering (validate.py-enforced).

from_component.description: The producer constituent's component_id (a sibling within this item; validate.py-enforced).

output.description: The producer's declared output name — a key of its Resource Type Spec's typed outputs (E2).

to_field.description: Dot-path on THIS constituent's spec that receives the value at dispatch time (the catalog-level form of the instance schema's binds_to bound_field).

failure_effect.description: How this constituent's failure affects the composite outcome — the §2.4 required_for_delivery classification (template-composition-model.md): required = halt + compensate (composite FAILED); partial = record, continue (composite DEGRADED); optional = note, ignore. Evaluated by the control plane, never by the registering provider (CMP-004).

spec_defaults.description: Free-form layer-assembled defaults for this constituent's spec — injected during the standard layer assembly phase (template-composition-model.md §7 step 3). Field values are typed by the constituent's Resource Type Spec, not re-validated here.

composition_visibility.description: How constituents surface as control-plane entities (template-composition-model.md §5): opaque = composite uuid only; transparent = every constituent is a first-class entity with a deterministic uuid (CMP-007); selective = only selective_visible constituents surface. ADDRESSABILITY, NOT ACCESS: this says whether a part HAS an identity you could refer to, never whether a given actor may READ it — a part can be fully addressable and still invisible to the person who ordered it, because access is decided by the grouping it lands in. Real visibility is addressability AND access; the second half is policy's, reading `composition.unreadable_constituents` (CMP-013).

selective_visible.description: Only when composition_visibility = selective: the component_ids surfaced as control-plane entities (template-composition-model.md §5). Must reference declared component_ids (registration-time check; not enforced by validate.py yet).
